items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I remember Richard Himber. [INTERVIEWEE] Richard Himber, there was Jack Sadey...

ctx.x: Richard Himber, there was Jack Sadey, Sleninsky, the guy that traveled around with the Boston Symphony with Bazhinsky (all phonetics) Freddie Fradkin and somebody else. They had four fiddles.
And Shaw was playing the clarinet.

items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I did a few things, what free lanced Himber... Oh, I worked for Dick Himber, I did a lot of things for Dick Himber on that little group he had called Studebaker Champion.

ctx.x: So then what happened. The war is over. The war ends that year.

I was living in Forestville. I bought a house out here, this place, that was 35 years ago? 1944. Well, then things -- there wasn't too much to be done then. I did a few things, what free lanced Himber, Bernie Green and radio and television and then I'm gradually getting out of the picture.
Still we have the 50's and 60's. What were you doing in the 50's and 60's.
